threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and initial backlog for the onboarding rollout.

messages.text: Kicking off the Hybrid Customer Onboarding Workspace Rollout project_title thread here. Goal is to standardize how we run onboarding across sales and project teams, using our existing tools only, and get the first pilot live within 21 days. I have drafted an outline for T1 and T2 and linked it to A1 so we can map as-is and to-be in one place. For this thread, we need to align on what is in scope vs out of scope and what success will look like, including which KPIs we track in A4 via T12. Please share any must-have or out-of-bounds items before we lock scope.

Thanks for opening this. From my side, I suggest we keep scope focused on the onboarding phase only: from signed deal to handover to steady-state customer success. Anything related to renewals or upsell motions should be out of scope for this rollout. For T1, I can help collect the current steps from recent projects and flag where we had delays or rework so they can be reflected in A1. On KPIs for A4 and T12, I would start with cycle time from contract signature to onboarding complete, number of handover issues, and number of missing documents per onboarding.

Agree with keeping renewals and upsell out of scope for now. I would also explicitly exclude any changes to the CRM data model; we should design the workflow in T2 to work with what we already have. For success criteria, I propose we define a target reduction in onboarding cycle time for the pilot, maybe a percentage improvement vs the baseline we capture in A4. We should also track adoption: how many onboarding cases actually use the new workspace structure once it is live.

From a risk angle, we should call out that we are not redesigning sales qualification or proposal steps. Scope starts once the opportunity is marked as closed-won in CRM. For T1, I can interview two recent project owners to document the as-is flow and pain points, then consolidate into A1. On KPIs in A4, in addition to cycle time and errors, I would like to track number of manual workarounds used, so we see where existing tools are not supporting the process well.

From the admin side, I suggest we keep billing and invoicing templates out of scope for this first rollout, and just make sure the onboarding workspace links to the existing invoice process. For T12 and A4, I can set up the tracking sheet with columns for cycle time, missing documents, and rework, and add a simple notes column so project managers can log any special cases. I will also need clarity on who will be responsible for updating the sheet per onboarding case.

Looking at this from a structure and compliance angle, I support the idea that we do not touch CRM configuration in this phase. However, we should include in scope the definition of how onboarding data is stored and shared in the workspace, so that later we can show legal and IT that we are following existing rules. That means T2 should already reference where documents live, and T12 and A4 should avoid capturing any sensitive personal data beyond what is already allowed. We should also clarify whether internal training content is in scope for this rollout or handled separately.

Good points. I suggest we keep internal training content in scope, but only as it relates to the new onboarding workflow and workspace, not broader sales training. That aligns with T8 and T9 later on. For now, in this thread, can we confirm that scope includes: mapping and redesigning the onboarding workflow and RACI, defining the shared workspace structure, creating templates and checklists, and setting up KPI tracking via T12 and A4. Out of scope: CRM data model changes, renewals and upsell processes, and redesign of billing templates. Does anyone see anything missing or disagree with this boundary before we record it as D1?

That scope works for me. One nuance: for the shared workspace, we should include basic access rules and naming conventions in scope, since that will impact how easy it is to find onboarding information later. We can document that in the same place as T2 or as a separate item linked to T5, but it should be clearly part of this rollout.

Agree with the scope and with adding access rules and naming conventions as part of the workspace definition. I would also explicitly say that we are not changing legal or data protection policies themselves, only making sure the onboarding process and templates comply with what already exists. That should help when we later send materials for review.

No objections from my side. I like the clarification that we are not changing policies, only aligning the process and workspace with them. For the KPI side, I recommend we keep the initial set small so teams actually fill in A4. Cycle time, number of missing documents, and number of rework loops should be enough for the pilot. We can always extend T12 later if needed.

I can work with that minimal KPI set. To keep it simple, I will pre-fill A4 with dropdowns where possible when I set up T12, so project managers only need to select values instead of typing free text. If we later add more KPIs, we can extend the sheet without breaking the initial data.

On success metrics, beyond the KPIs in A4, I suggest we define a qualitative success statement for the pilot: for example, that all stakeholders involved in the pilot can find the latest onboarding documents in the shared workspace without asking around. We can capture that via a short internal survey after T10.

This is helpful. Let me summarize what I am hearing so we can close D1 and D2. Scope includes: mapping current onboarding (T1), designing the target hybrid workflow and RACI (T2), defining the shared workspace structure and rules (T5), configuring the pilot workspace (T6), creating templates and checklists, and setting up KPI tracking (T12 with A4). Out of scope: CRM data model changes, renewals and upsell, redesign of billing templates, and changes to legal or data protection policies. Success metrics for the pilot: reduction in onboarding cycle time vs baseline, fewer missing documents and rework loops, and evidence that teams can find onboarding materials in the workspace without confusion. KPIs in A4 for T12: cycle time, number of missing documents, number of rework loops, and optional notes. If there are no strong objections, I will record this as our scope and KPI decision.
Summary looks good to me. With that in place, I can start scheduling the interviews for T1 and make sure we capture the baseline cycle time so we have something to compare against in A4.
Aligned from my side as well. Once T1 gives us the as-is view in A1, I will support on T2 to make sure the target workflow and RACI reflect the agreed scope and KPIs.
No further comments. When you move into T2 and T5, please loop me in so we can ensure the workspace structure and data handling are consistent with our existing legal and IT expectations.
I will wait for the first outputs from T1 and T2 so that T12 and A4 match the final workflow steps and terminology. Once those are available, I can draft the sheet and share a link here for review.
All good from my side. I will help validate that the KPIs in A4 are easy to capture during the pilot so we do not create extra admin work for the teams.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the target onboarding workflow, RACI, and workspace structure.

messages.text: As a follow-up to the scope alignment, I have uploaded a first draft of the target hybrid onboarding workflow and RACI into A1 and a separate proposal for the shared workspace structure aligned with T5. The workflow covers from closed-won to handover to customer success, with clear swimlanes for sales, project management, and customer success. For the workspace, I suggested a standard folder and channel layout that we can later use when we configure the pilot in T6 and raise the IT request in A8 if needed. Please review and comment so we can converge on D3 and D4 for pilot use.

I went through the workflow in A1. Overall it looks clear. One question: in the step where sales hands over to project management, you have both teams responsible for updating the workspace. To avoid confusion, I would suggest making project management responsible and sales consulted in the RACI. That way, when we configure the pilot workspace in T6, there is a single owner for keeping the structure up to date.

On the RACI in A1, I noticed that customer success is only informed for most steps. For the pilot, I would make them consulted on the configuration of customer-facing materials, since they often see where onboarding creates confusion later. That might mean adding them as consulted on the checklist creation step and on the final review before handover.

For the workspace structure in the T5 proposal, I like the idea of having a standard top-level folder per customer with subfolders for contract, onboarding, and operations. For the onboarding subfolder, could we standardize names like 01-Intake, 02-Configuration, 03-Training, 04-Handover. That will make it easier to compare across customers and to pull data later if we need to.

Looking at the workspace proposal in A6, I would add a dedicated place for standard templates and checklists, separate from customer-specific folders. That way, when we update templates later, we do not have to touch each customer workspace. Maybe a shared Templates area linked from each onboarding workspace, so T3 and T7 outputs are easy to find.

I reviewed both the workflow in A1 and the workspace structure in A6. From a structure and compliance perspective, the main thing I would adjust is to separate internal notes from customer-facing documents in the onboarding folder. For example, under 02-Configuration, we could have Internal and Customer subfolders. That will reduce the risk of sharing internal notes by mistake. Also, for T5, we should define a simple naming rule for each onboarding workspace, such as CustomerName-Onboarding-YYYY, and confirm with IT via A8 that this works with our existing tools.

Thanks all for the feedback. I will update A1 to reflect project management as responsible and sales as consulted for the workspace update step, and add customer success as consulted on customer-facing materials. For the workspace in A6 and T5, I will incorporate the standardized subfolder names and the separation between internal and customer-facing content, plus the naming convention CustomerName-Onboarding-YYYY. Once updated, I will share again here before we lock D3 and D4.

One more detail on the workflow in A1: can we explicitly include a step for confirming tool access for all internal stakeholders before onboarding starts. That will tie into T6 when we configure the pilot workspace and make sure no one is blocked on day one.

Agree with the changes. Could we also add a simple decision point in the workflow for whether a customer needs a custom onboarding path or can follow the standard one. That will help us keep the standard path clean while still allowing exceptions when justified.

On the workspace naming convention in A6, I would suggest we also include a short internal code for the region if that matters for access rules. For example, CustomerName-Onboarding-Region-YYYY. We can check with IT via A8 if there are any length limits.

For the standard subfolders under onboarding, could we also add 00-Intake-Checklist as a place to store the completed checklists from T7. That will make it easier to audit later and to see at a glance what has been completed for each customer.

I like the idea of including region in the naming convention, as long as we keep it short and standardized, for example EU, US, APAC. That should not cause issues with IT, but I will double-check when we validate T5 via A8. On the workflow side, the decision point for custom vs standard onboarding should be early, ideally right after intake, so we do not duplicate work.

I have now updated A1 and A6 based on all comments: project management responsible for workspace updates, customer success consulted on customer-facing materials, explicit tool access check before onboarding starts, early decision point for custom vs standard path, standardized onboarding subfolders including 00-Intake-Checklist, and workspace naming convention CustomerName-Onboarding-Region-YYYY with short region codes. For T5, I also documented basic access rules per role. Unless there are blocking concerns, I propose we approve this workflow and RACI for pilot use and confirm the workspace structure and naming conventions as our standard for the rollout.
Looks good to me. With D3 and D4 in place, I can start preparing T6 for the pilot customer using the approved structure and naming rules.
Aligned from my side. The RACI in A1 is clear and should help avoid confusion during the pilot. I will use it as the basis when we brief stakeholders.
No further comments. Once IT confirms via A8 that the naming and access rules are feasible, we should be ready to go for T6.
Thanks for clarifying the folder structure in A6. I will align the template and checklist locations with this so that T3 and T7 outputs fit naturally into the workspace.
Confirmed from my side as well. I will reach out to IT to validate T5 details via A8 and flag any constraints, but I do not expect major issues with the current design.

threads.thread_goal: Create and validate templates, checklists, and compliance aspects.

messages.text: I have drafted initial versions of the onboarding document and email templates for T3 and uploaded them into A5, and also created first-pass internal checklists for sales, project, and customer success for T7, now stored in A3. The templates follow the new workflow steps from A1 and use the folder structure from A6. I also started a skeleton for the quick-start guideline in A2, but it still needs more detail from project management. Please review the wording, missing steps, and any compliance concerns before we send them for formal review under T4.

Thanks for pulling these together. I went through the project manager checklist in A3 and the main onboarding email templates in A5. Overall they align with the workflow in A1. One gap I noticed is that the project checklist does not explicitly include the tool access confirmation step we added in the workflow. We should add that as a mandatory item before scheduling any customer sessions.

On the sales checklist in A3, I would add a step to confirm that the signed contract and key scope details are stored in the Contract subfolder before we start onboarding. That will avoid confusion later. For the customer welcome email in A5, maybe we can simplify the wording a bit and clearly list the next three steps so customers know what to expect.

I checked the customer success checklist in A3. It looks good, but I would add a final verification step to confirm that all customer-facing materials used during onboarding are stored in the Customer subfolders defined in A6. That will help with consistency and later audits.

On A2, the quick-start guide, I suggest we structure it around the main phases from A1: Intake, Configuration, Training, Handover. For each phase, we can link to the relevant checklist in A3 and templates in A5. That way, new team members can follow the flow without reading the full process document.

From a compliance perspective, I scanned the templates in A5 and the draft guide in A2. We should avoid asking for any sensitive personal data in the standard forms unless it is strictly necessary and already covered by existing policies. For example, in the intake form, we can focus on role, contact details, and system requirements, and leave anything more sensitive out. Before we send A5 and A3 for formal review under T4, I recommend we add a short section in A2 reminding staff not to store sensitive data outside approved systems.

Thanks for the feedback. I will update A3 to add the tool access confirmation, contract storage, and final verification steps, and adjust the welcome email in A5 to highlight the next three steps more clearly. I will also add a short reminder in A2 about not storing sensitive data outside approved systems, as suggested.

Once those edits are in, I can help flesh out A2 under T8 with screenshots of the workspace structure from A6 and examples of how to complete the checklists in A3. That will make the guide more practical for the pilot teams.

Before we send A3 and A5 to legal and compliance under T4, should we add a short cover note explaining that these are for the hybrid onboarding process only and that we are not changing any underlying policies. That might speed up their review.

Good idea. I can draft that cover note and reference the relevant sections of our existing policies, then attach it when we submit A3 and A5 for review under T4. That should make it clear that we are aligning with current rules, not proposing changes.

On the checklists in A3, could we add a simple escalation note for each team, pointing to who they should contact if they hit a blocker during onboarding. That can also be reflected in A2 under T8 so people know where to go for help.

For the customer-facing templates in A5, I suggest we keep a neutral tone and avoid promising specific timelines until we have confirmed them internally. Maybe we can phrase it as we will share a detailed schedule after the intake call, which aligns with the workflow in A1.

I have now applied the requested changes to A3, A5, and A2: added the missing steps and escalation notes to the checklists, simplified and clarified the welcome email, and structured the quick-start guide around the main phases with links to the relevant artifacts. Unless there are any last-minute issues, I think we are ready to send A3 and A5 to legal and compliance under T4.

I will go ahead and submit A3 and A5 to legal and compliance as part of T4, with the cover note we discussed. I will track their feedback and share any required changes here so we can keep a clear record of what was adjusted.

Once we receive feedback from legal and compliance, we should incorporate it into A3, A5, and A2 and then formally confirm that these are the standard templates and checklists for the pilot. That will allow us to close D5 and D6 with a clear audit trail.

Update from legal and compliance: they reviewed A3 and A5 and requested only minor wording changes to the data protection notice in the customer-facing templates. I have incorporated their comments and they have now provided written confirmation that the templates and checklists comply with existing requirements. With that, I believe we can consider T4 complete and record that A3, A5, and A2 are approved for pilot use.
Great, with D5 and D6 in place, we can start using A3 and A5 in the pilot configuration under T6 and T10. I will make sure the pilot team is aware that these are the approved versions.
I will also reference A2 during the training session planning so that staff know exactly which templates and checklists to use during the pilot.
Thanks for closing the loop with legal and compliance. I will tidy up the folder where A3 and A5 live and make sure the version-controlled structure is clear for everyone before we start the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate the pilot onboarding execution and training.

messages.text: Time to align on the pilot. I propose we use the upcoming onboarding for a mid-size customer as our first pilot case. They are starting in about 10 days, which fits our 21-day window. I can configure the pilot workspace under T6 using the approved structure from A6 and raise any IT needs via A8. For training, we need to decide whether to run a live session, record a walkthrough, or both, using A2 as the base. Let us use this thread to confirm the pilot customer and start date, and agree on the training format so we can close D7 and D8.

Using that mid-size customer makes sense to me: they are complex enough to test the workflow but not so large that we risk major disruption. Their contract is already signed, and the planned onboarding start is next Monday. If we confirm them as the pilot customer, we should aim to have T6 completed and training delivered under T9 by the end of this week.

I agree with that customer as the pilot candidate. They have a cooperative team and are used to remote collaboration, which should help us test the hybrid aspects. On training, I would lean toward one live session for the core pilot team plus a recorded walkthrough based on A2 for anyone who cannot attend.

From a risk perspective, that customer is a good test because they involve both office-based and remote stakeholders. For training under T9, I support the combination of a live session and a recording. We should also include a short Q and A segment in the live session to capture any early concerns.

For the pilot workspace in T6, once you create it using A6, please let me know where to place the standard templates and checklists so that the pilot team can easily find A3 and A5. I can also help with a short segment in the training to show where to log KPIs in A4.

Before we lock the pilot start date, we should confirm with IT via A8 that all required access rights can be set up in time for T6. If there is any delay, we might need to adjust the training schedule under T9 so that people are not trained on a workspace they cannot access.

I will raise the IT request in A8 today and ask them to confirm access setup by Thursday. Assuming they agree, we can keep the onboarding start date as next Monday. For training, I propose a 60-minute live session on Friday morning, recorded and then shared along with A2.

That schedule works for me. I can co-host the live training under T9 and walk through the workflow in A1 and the quick-start guide in A2, while you demo the pilot workspace from T6. We will record the session and link it in the channel for anyone who cannot join.

I will make sure the sales and customer success reps for this pilot customer block time for the Friday training. For the recording, we should also capture a short segment on how to update A4 during the pilot so that KPI tracking under T10 is consistent.
During the live session, I can take notes on any questions or concerns raised and later feed them into T10 so that the pilot report captures early feedback, not just end-of-onboarding observations.
I can prepare a short demo of A4 for the training, showing how to log cycle time, missing documents, and rework loops. That should make it easier for the team to keep the sheet updated during T10.

Please also remind the team during training not to store any sensitive data in A4 or in unapproved parts of the workspace. We can reference the reminder in A2 so that this is consistent with what legal and compliance approved.

IT has now confirmed via A8 that they can set up access for the pilot workspace by Thursday. Given that, I propose we formally confirm this mid-size customer as our pilot and keep the onboarding start date as next Monday, with the live training on Friday morning and a recording shared afterward. Unless there are objections, we can record this as D7 and D8.
Confirmed from my side. I will finalize the training agenda under T9 using A2 and coordinate invites for the core pilot team.
All good. I will brief the sales and customer success reps so they know this onboarding will follow the new hybrid process and that we will be collecting feedback as part of T10.

I will prepare a simple template for capturing qualitative feedback during the pilot and attach it to the T10 activities so that we have both quantitative KPIs from A4 and narrative input from the team.
I will make sure A4 is ready and linked from the pilot workspace before the training, so people can see where to log data during T10.
No objections. I will stay available during the first week of the pilot in case any structural or access issues arise with the workspace configured under T6.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results, adjust process, and agree on rollout plan.

messages.text: We have completed the pilot onboarding for the selected customer. I have uploaded the Pilot Onboarding Summary Report to A7 and updated the KPI snapshot in A4 based on T10. In short, cycle time improved by around 20 percent compared to our baseline, missing documents were reduced, but we saw some confusion around where to store certain customer-facing materials and a few delays in updating A4. Let us use this thread to review the findings, agree on key changes to the workflow and templates, and decide whether we proceed with a broader rollout now or need another pilot, so we can close D9 and D10.

I went through A7 and the KPIs in A4. The improvements in cycle time and reduction in missing documents are encouraging. The main issues seem to be around workspace navigation and the effort required to keep A4 updated. For T11, I suggest we focus changes on clarifying folder naming for customer-facing materials in A6 and simplifying the data entry in A4, rather than altering the core workflow in A1, which seems to have worked well.

From the qualitative feedback in A7, teams appreciated having a single workspace but asked for clearer guidance on which subfolder to use for drafts versus final versions. Maybe we can adjust A2 and A3 under T11 to include a simple rule, such as always storing final customer-facing documents in the Customer subfolder and drafts in Internal.

On A4, some project managers mentioned that logging every rework loop was time-consuming. For the broader rollout, we could simplify by only tracking whether rework occurred at least once per onboarding, instead of counting each loop. That would still give us a useful signal without adding too much admin overhead.

I noticed that some teams were not sure where to find A3 and A5 inside the workspace during the pilot. For T11, I can adjust the folder layout in A6 slightly and add a prominent Templates and Checklists link at the top of each onboarding workspace. I can also tweak A2 to show a screenshot of where that link is.

From a structure and compliance angle, A7 shows that there were no incidents related to data handling, which is good. However, the confusion about where to store customer-facing materials suggests we should tighten the guidance in A6 and A2. I support the idea of clearly separating drafts and final versions and making that visible in the folder names. We should also keep the reminder about not storing sensitive data in A4, as that worked well.

I like the suggestion to simplify rework tracking in A4. For T11, we can change the column from number of rework loops to a simple yes or no plus an optional comment. That should reduce friction while still giving us insight into where the process is not smooth.

Given the pilot results in A7 and the feedback here, I propose the following focus areas for T11: minor adjustments to A6 and A2 to clarify folder usage and navigation, simplification of A4 as discussed, and small wording tweaks in A3 and A5 where the pilot surfaced confusion. I do not see a need for major changes to the core workflow in A1. If we agree, we can implement these changes quickly and then move to a broader rollout rather than running another full pilot.

I agree with that approach. The pilot results in A7 are strong enough that I do not think we need another pilot. As long as we implement the targeted improvements under T11, I would support moving to a phased rollout across new customers.

Same here. The main risks identified in A7 seem manageable with the tweaks we discussed. I would suggest we start the broader rollout with a few additional customers over the next month, monitor A4 closely, and then decide if any further adjustments are needed.

I can handle the updates to A4 and help adjust the folder layout in A6 as part of T11. Once done, I will share a short change log in the channel so everyone knows what changed before we roll out more broadly.

I will review the proposed changes to A6 and A2 to ensure they remain aligned with our legal and IT expectations. Given that there were no compliance issues in A7, I am comfortable moving to a broader rollout after T11, as long as we keep monitoring for any new patterns.

I will take care of implementing the changes to A3 and A5 under T11, based on the specific issues highlighted in A7. Once those are updated, we can freeze the templates for the next wave of customers.

Based on the data in A4 and the analysis in A7, plus the feedback here, I propose we formally agree on the following for D9 and D10: for D9, we will implement targeted improvements under T11 to A6, A2, A4, A3, and A5 as discussed, without changing the core workflow in A1. For D10, we will proceed with a broader rollout to all new onboarding cases starting next month, using the updated materials, while monitoring KPIs in A4 and capturing any further lessons in follow-up reviews.
I support that plan. I will coordinate with sales and customer success so that all new deals starting next month follow the new onboarding process and use the updated workspace and templates.
Aligned from my side as well. I will help monitor A4 during the first month of the broader rollout and flag any trends that suggest we need another adjustment cycle.
I will implement the A4 and A6 updates under T11 this week and share the change log once done, so everyone is ready for the broader rollout.
No objections. I will stay involved during the first month of the rollout to ensure any structural or compliance-related issues are addressed quickly.
I will coordinate T11 activities and update A7 with a short addendum once the changes are implemented, so we have a complete record of how the pilot informed the final design.
